extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, assignees, and USPTO staff (Assignment Recordation Branch / examiners)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for recording assignments, licenses, security interests, notices (e.g., arbitration awards), correcting recorded assignment records, and establishing an assignee's right to take action in patent matters (pre‑AIA context highlighted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Government License Rights statement placement
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Government License Rights' statement must be included within the specification of an application per 35 U.S.C. 202(c)(6). The 'Government License Rights' statement should follow immediately as the second paragraph of the specification; if there is no such paragraph the statement should appear as the first paragraph of the specification. Providing information on a provisional application cover sheet does not satisfy the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.77(b)(1)-(3). The statement must be in the specification of the application and any patent issuing thereon, specifying that the invention was made with Government support and that the Government has certain rights in the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and content of notice of arbitration awards (35 U.S.C. 294 / 37 CFR 1.335)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an arbitrator issues an award under 35 U.S.C. 294, the patentee, assignee, or licensee must file written notice of the award in the Patent Office for each patent involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must set forth the patent number, the names of the inventor and patent owner, and the names and addresses of the parties to the arbitration, and must include a copy of the award. If the award is modified by a court, a notice of the modification and a copy of the court’s order modifying the award must be filed. An award is unenforceable until the required notice is received by the Director. Direct notices to the Office of the Solicitor; the Office of the Solicitor will process such notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration awards enforceability rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An arbitrator's award is final and binding between the parties but has no force or effect on any other person; the award is unenforceable until notice required by subsection (d) is received by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may agree that a court judgment of invalidity may allow modification of the award by a court; any such modification governs rights and obligations between arbitration parties from the modification date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of documents accepted for recording (licenses, security interests, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request, assignments of applications, patents, and registrations and other documents relating to interests in patent applications and patents (typical examples: license agreements, agreements conveying a security interest) will be recorded in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents are recorded to give third parties notification of equitable interests or other matters relevant to ownership. Some documents (e.g., attorney's liens) are not accepted for recording. See 35 U.S.C. 261 and 37 CFR 3.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation is not determinative of title or document validity
rubrics_metrics.description: The recordation of a document is not a determination of the effect of the document on the chain of title or the validity of the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will determine what effect, if any, a document has on title when ownership must be established to permit action by a purported assignee. See MPEP §§ 324 and 325; see also Realvirt, LLC v. Lee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required items for recordation submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Each request for recordation must include the document to be recorded, a completed cover sheet (see 37 CFR 3.31 and MPEP § 302.07), and the appropriate recording fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the document involves more than one patent, a separate notice/recordation is required for each patent. The Office will assign a new recording date, update the assignment database, and include the cover sheet and document as part of the official record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing/cross-referencing additional patent/application numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to 'index' or 'cross-reference' additional patent or application numbers against a document (other than an assignment) are not processed unless accompanied by the document, a completed cover sheet, and the appropriate fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests must comply with 37 CFR 3.11, 3.28, and 3.31 and include the document to be recorded and a cover sheet; otherwise they will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment Recordation Branch formal examination and returns
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents and cover sheets submitted for recording are examined for formal requirements to separate recordable from non-recordable documents. Documents considered not recordable are returned to the sender with an explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sender believes the document is an unusual case justifying recordation, they may petition the Director under 37 CFR 1.181 requesting recordation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording date: when established and effect of returned/corrected papers (37 CFR 3.51)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of recording is the date the document meeting the requirements for recording is filed in the Office. Documents not complying with identification, cover sheet, or fee requirements will be returned for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned papers are stamped with original receipt date; if corrected and resubmitted within the time specified in the return letter, the Office will consider the original date of filing as the date of recording. If not resubmitted in time the corrected papers’ receipt date is the date of recording. The specified period to resubmit will not be extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of recording: limitations and Office determination (37 CFR 3.54)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recording under § 3.11 is not a determination of the validity of the document or its effect on title; the Office will determine effect when necessary, including whether a party has authority to act in a pending matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This serves as notification that recordation preserves a history of claimed interests but does not itself adjudicate title questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional assignments treated as absolute for Office purposes (37 CFR 3.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments conditional on future acts or events (e.g., payment) that are recorded are regarded as absolute assignments for Office purposes until canceled with written consent of all parties or by court decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office does not determine whether the condition has been fulfilled; the submission of such an assignment for recordation is treated as signifying that the act/event has occurred. A security agreement that does not convey title is not a conditional assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent purchaser rule and untimely recordation (35 U.S.C. 261)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an assignment is not timely recorded at the USPTO, the unrecorded assignment will not be superior to rights acquired by a third party (a bona fide purchaser for valuable consideration) if that third party did not have knowledge of the unrecorded assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to record can harm priority of rights. See CMS Industries, Inc. v. L.P.S. International.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where assignment documents should be placed (not in patent/application files)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment documents submitted for recording should not be placed directly in application or patent files but forwarded to the Assignment Recordation Branch for recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the official assignment records and prevents improper placement in prosecution files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title reports: purpose and access
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'title report' is a form used within certain Office circumstances (e.g., Reexamination Preprocessing Staff) to report the owner of an application or patent as shown by Assignment Recordation Branch records on the report date; title reports may not be ordered by applicants or attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may obtain a title report via the Patent Data Portal (Assignments search). The public can request a certified abstract of title for the fee set in 37 CFR 1.19(b)(4). See MPEP § 301.01 for which records are publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective document required to fix errors in recorded assignment document
rubrics_metrics.description: An error in a recorded assignment document will be corrected provided a 'corrective document' is submitted that includes (A) a copy of the original assignment with corrections made therein and initialed and dated by the party conveying the interest, and (B) a new Recordation Form Cover Sheet (PTO-1595) identifying the submission as a 'corrective document' and indicating the reel and frame number where the incorrect document appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corrective document will be recorded, given a new reel/frame number and recording date, and the recording fee is required for each patent/application being corrected. Corrections may be made on the original assignment document (e.g., lining out an incorrect patent number). Recorded documents will generally not be expunged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet correction criteria (37 CFR 3.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: An error in a cover sheet recorded pursuant to § 3.11 will be corrected only if (1) the error is apparent when the cover sheet is compared with the recorded document to which it pertains and (2) a corrected cover sheet is filed for recordation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corrected cover sheet must be accompanied by a copy of the originally submitted document and the recording fee. The Assignment Recordation Branch records cover sheet data exactly as submitted and does not compare the cover sheet to the document during initial recording; parties should carefully review the notice of recordation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling typographical errors in cover sheet that do not affect title
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recorded cover sheet contains a typographical error that does not affect title to the application or patent, the Assignment Recordation Branch will correct the Assignment Historical Database and permit the recording party to keep the original date of recordation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The party should submit the originally recorded assignment document (or copy), a corrected cover sheet, and the required fee. Provide original cover sheet for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling typographical errors in cover sheet that affect title
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original cover sheet contains a typographical error that affects title to the application or patent, the recording party will not be entitled to keep the original date of recordation; the Assignment Recordation Branch will correct automated records and change the date of recordation to the date the corrected cover sheet was received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit corrected cover sheet, original document copy, and required fees; original date is lost when title-affecting error corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of errors in recorded assignment documents when assignor unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is an error in the recorded assignment document rather than the cover sheet and the assignor is not available to correct or execute a new document, the assignee may submit an affidavit or declaration identifying the error and requesting correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit/declaration must be accompanied by a copy of the originally recorded papers, a cover sheet, and the required fee for each patent/application to be corrected. See cases such as In re Abacab Intl. Computers Ltd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when another person improperly recorded an assignment or name change
rubrics_metrics.description: If the owner discovers another party improperly recorded an assignment or name change against the owner's application or patent, the owner must correct the error by having a corrected cover sheet filed; if the other party cannot be located or declines, the true owner must record the necessary papers with the Assignment Recordation Branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a completed cover sheet identifying the application/patent, an affidavit/declaration (identifying correct owner, stating erroneous submission, providing reel/frame number), and the required fee. The affidavit should include a summary of true chain of title and state that the original applicant/patentee or last correct assignee remains the owner. On the corrected cover sheet check 'Other' and indicate the submission is to correct an error; write the correct owner in both conveying and receiving party boxes to show ownership never changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement of assignment records: rare and strict standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to 'expunge' or redact assignment records are rarely granted and will not result in removal of a document image from the assignment records; petitioners must prove (A) that normal corrective procedures will not provide adequate relief and (B) that the integrity of the assignment records will not be affected by granting the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if granted, the image remains at the same reel/frame but links to the application/patent are deleted in the Assignment Historical Database; a redacted version must be recorded and may be supplemented by an additional assignment where necessary. Petitions involving redaction other than PII are considered to affect record integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing right of assignee to take action in pre‑AIA applications (37 CFR 3.71 / 3.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor is presumed owner unless there is an assignment. An assignee must establish ownership to the satisfaction of the Director to request or take action in patent matters. For pre‑AIA applications, assignees who may conduct prosecution are (1) a single assignee of the entire right, title and interest, or (2) partial assignees together or with inventor(s) who together own the entire right, title and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership is established by a signed statement identifying the assignee, accompanied by either (i) documentary evidence of a chain of title (copy of executed assignment) or (ii) a statement specifying where the documentary evidence is recorded (e.g., reel/frame). The submission must show the signer is authorized to act on behalf of the assignee (a statement that signer is authorized or signature by person with apparent authority). For patent matters the establishment must be submitted prior to or at the same time as the paper requesting action. If assignee owns less than entire interest, indicate extent (by percentage) or Office may refuse acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must join in taking action when multiple owners exist
rubrics_metrics.description: When ownership is split (partial assignees and/or inventors retaining rights), all parties having any portion of ownership must join in 'taking action' (act together as a composite entity) to be entitled to conduct prosecution, unless a petition under pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.47 has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition under 1.47 granted, assignee need only be assignee of the entire interest of the 1.47 applicant to sign a power of attorney. Examples and further specifics provided in MPEP subsections (e.g., reissue/inventorship correction context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions owners/assignees may take in patent matters (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or assignees (for pre‑AIA applications) can in numerous instances take actions such as signing a reply to an Office action, filing a request for a continued prosecution application, filing a terminal disclaimer, submitting fee transmittal, requesting status of an application, appointing their own registered practitioner to prosecute, granting a power to inspect, consenting to a reissue application, and consenting to correction of inventorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific MPEP sections govern each action (see cited MPEP §§: 201.06(d), 1490, 1306, 102, 409.03(b), 402.07, 104, 1410.01, 602.01(c), 1481). Effective Sept 16, 2012, additional representation/signature rules apply to juristic entities (see MPEP discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation requirement for juristic entities (post‑Sept 16, 2012 note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective Sept 16, 2012, an owner or assignee who is a juristic entity must be represented by a patent practitioner for most papers; certain items (e.g., small entity assertions, disclaimers under 37 CFR 1.321, submissions under 37 CFR 3.73 to establish ownership, powers of attorney, and powers to inspect) have specified handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juristic entities may sign certain narrow papers themselves (MPEP § references), but otherwise papers submitted on behalf of a juristic entity on or after Sept 16, 2012 must be signed by a patent practitioner (see 37 CFR 1.31 and related MPEP discussion).
